result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers correctly decline the unsupported comparisons, state 19 of 24 and 11 of 24 precisely, and build the case from small groups, qualified teachers, 90-minute weekly sessions and half-term notes. B's paragraph says outright that 'Those results come from small-group teaching', which is the causal overclaim the rubric warns against. A hedges this with 'We think this comes from how we teach', and its notes explain why. B adds useful pre-publishing checks, but its placeholder parent quote adds clutter and doesn't make up for the causal claim. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers drop the unsupported city-average and franchise claims and give the 19-of-24 and 11-improved figures exactly, with the right base. A's draft says 'Those results come from small-group teaching', which credits the centre alone with the results. B hedges this with 'we think this comes from how we teach'. B also makes a warmer, more persuasive case by explaining why small groups help: students have time to ask questions and gaps get spotted early.
